---
title: "Why MTL-101"
date: "2026-09-17"
categories: [overview]
description: "The question this project starts from, what already exists to answer it, and what is left to build."
toc: false
---

Every school finder in Montreal answers the same question: type in an address, get the school
that serves it. A parent who has not yet chosen where to live needs the opposite. They have a
sense of the school they want, a francophone public elementary school with a particular program
or a particular profile, and they need to know which neighbourhoods put that school within reach.
MTL-101 starts from that reversed question, for the island of Montreal only: the CSSDM, the
CSS Marguerite-Bourgeoys and the CSS Pointe-de-l'Île, with the West Island, the South Shore and
Laval left out.

Much of the raw material already exists. The CSSDM runs a searchable school finder, the Ministry
publishes an interactive map of every school network, and its socioeconomic deprivation indices
(the IMSE and SFR) are open data on Données Québec, refreshed annually, downloadable as CSV and
GeoJSON. What none of these do is put the pieces together: reconcile a zone lookup with the
deprivation decile, notice that a school has been relocated during a renovation, tell apart two
schools with the same name under different boards, or say whether a program admits by lottery,
by dossier, or by address. The posts here document that synthesis as it is built, starting with
what the government data actually contains and where it falls short.
